title: Oleksandr Usyk vacates his three world heavyweight titles: What comes next?
content:
Oleksandr Usyk has vacated his three world heavyweight titles as he nears retirement but insists he is not finished in the sport yet.

The 39-year-old — widely regarded as the best heavyweight of this era and unbeaten in 25 professional fights — had given up the WBO title earlier this year having twice reigned as undisputed champion. The Ukrainian confirmed on Friday that he has now relinquished the WBC, WBA and IBF belts too.

However, he says he still has a “last dance” to come despite the move to vacate his crown.

“This is a well-considered decision that I am confident will open new opportunities for me. This is not the end of the story. The continuation lies ahead,” he said in a video posted on X.

“I want to vacate all the belts that I currently hold to make them available for the guys next in line to fight for them. Friends, I’m leaving the belts but not the sport because I still have my last dance.”

Usyk was given a scare by kickboxer Rico Verhoeven, who had competed only once in boxing previously, before finding a stoppage late in the 11th round in his previous outing and a rematch has been mooted.

The Ukrainian has won gold at world, European and Olympic level as an amateur before turning professional and becoming undisputed champion at cruiserweight before repeating the feat twice at heavyweight to make him a certain future hall of fame member.

His record includes two wins over both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua while their fellow Brit Daniel Dubois, who currently holds the WBO title, has also been beaten twice by the Ukrainian.

This is the beginning of the end for one of the all-time greats of the sport.

Usyk giving up the belts means he will now be considered as the current best in the division by reputation only rather than his title collection.

By giving up the belts, he removes himself from the mandatory merry-go-round and can now decide for himself what the ‘last dance’ will be to bring down the curtain on a remarkable career.

What Usyk giving up the belts means for the division is that it is now wide open for other contenders to stake their claim to take over Usyk’s throne. Since he moved to heavyweight and took three titles from Joshua in 2021, the division has revolved around the Ukrainian’s moves.

When title holders have multiple belts, mandatories are decided on a rotational basis. The WBC was next with ‘interim’ champion Agit Kabayel patiently waiting for over a year for his shot at the full title. The German is now expected to be elevated to champion but the WBC are yet to confirm this.

Fury is ranked as the No 1 contender with the WBC but is heading for a fight with Joshua later this year so is not expected to challenge Kabayel. Sources close to the Fury and Joshua negotiations do not expect, at this stage, for a world title to be on the line when the two British fighters meet but have indicated that “things can change quickly in boxing”.

There is expected to be a push from Frank Warren’s Queensberry Promotions to get one of the world titles on the line for the August 29 fight between Britain’s Moses Itauma and Croatia’s Filip Hrgovic. Itauma and Hrgovic are ranked No. 3 and No. 4 with the International Boxing Federation.

Cuban Frank Sanchez is No. 1 so a deal would need to be negotiated for the sanctioning body to allow that to happen. Itauma, 21, is also ranked No. 1 with the WBA which means he is well positioned to take over from Usyk in the coming 12 months. In boxing’s bizarre ways, Russian Murat Gassiev holds a lesser version of the WBA title so may be upgraded to full champion.

Dubois is also in a strong position as WBO champion but he first faces a rematch with Fabio Wardley later this year before he can try to unify titles.

Usyk may not be retiring now but the end is near for one of the sport’s true greats and now the scramble to follow in his footsteps really begins.
